question.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=2$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $4$ | $-3$ | $2$ | $5$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=2.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=2}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=2} & =f(2){g}^{′}(2)+g(2){f}^{′}(2) \\  & =(4)(5)+(-3)(2) \\  & =20-6 \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$
